citation: "Chicago River." Wikipedia. Quoting Lt. James Strode Swearingen's 1803 description of the river at Fort Dearborn and the 1833-37 harbour works.
note: A finding aid, not evidence. What matters here is the figure it carries from Swearingen 1803: the river at Fort Dearborn about 30 yards (90 ft) wide and upwards of 18 ft deep, with banks 8 ft high on the south side and 6 ft on the north. Also: the pre-reversal flow was sluggish and outward into the lake with a near-zero surface gradient, which is what licenses a flat water surface at the datum through the whole downtown reach. Both figures are measured at the FORT, roughly 1.2 miles downstream of the forks — do not carry them to the forks without saying so. Chase Swearingen to a primary printing before promoting anything derived from it to documented.
